item: is_watching_fixture: +0x3f "competition"/+0 "club" are .time_slice()/.comp_id(); human_manager_record::WATCHED_FIXTURE comment says HOME_CLUB_ID but compared to comp_id
evidence: The record holds a copy of the whole fixture starting at 0x9ad4: 0x9ad4+0 comp id (compared with .comp_id()), +0xc = 0x9ae0 home club id, +0x10 = 0x9ae4 away club id, +0x28 = 0x9afc year, +0x2a = 0x9afe day, +0x34 = 0x9b08 round number, +0x3f = 0x9b13 time slice: every offset matches fixture:: exactly. So +0x3f is TIME_SLICE and +0 is COMP_ID; the header swapped them with 'competition'/'club'.

item: 0x2db0 has two names: commentary_queue::VOLUME and match_events_fields::COMMENTARY_SPEED
evidence: Same object: construct_commentary_queue builds the object that engine::COMMENTATOR points to, and match_screens/match_day read +0x2db0 on engine::COMMENTATOR. The value is the match-screen speed setting: handle_match_screen_input writes the menu item value there and passes it to HUMAN_MANAGER::set_commentary_speed (community name); match_day 1586 waits 0 ms when it is 20; the event sound length is weight x value / 100 and the sound plays only at >= 101. 125 at construction is the default speed. Nothing treats it as a loudness. Keep match_events_fields::COMMENTARY_SPEED (it should probably be merged into commentary_queue, the same object).
uses_to_recheck: match_events.rs 697 header: 'with volume (`commentary_queue::VOLUME` >= 101)' -> 'with a commentary speed (`commentary_queue::COMMENTARY_SPEED`) of 101 or more'
match_events.rs 1060, 1080 (local named volume: reads fine as speed factor, rename optional)
match_screens.rs 463 and 740 headers call COMMENTARY_SPEED 'the commentator volume': should say 'the commentary speed'

item: intl_date_entry::WEEKDAY (+1) gets the day in build_international_date_table: maybe swapped
evidence: resolve_international_dates calls Date::set (0x54a130) with arg1 = byte +1, arg2 = MONTH (+2), arg3 = year, arg5 = byte +0. Disassembly of 0x54a130: arg1 is checked 1..31 (day of month), arg2 0..11 (month), and the 5th arg goes to 0x54a2d0, which computes the weekday of the date (mod 7) and moves the date to the nearest target weekday (FN_DATE_GET_WEEKDAY is 0x54a3f0 nearby). The INTERNATIONAL_DATES table has column 0 in 0..6 and column 1 in 1..29. So +0 is the weekday and +1 the day of month. Rename order: WEEKDAY -> DAY first, then WEEK -> WEEKDAY. Uses: friendly.rs 823 (writes `dia` into it: reads right as DAY), records.rs 13051-13066 accessors week()/weekday() -> weekday()/day().
also: friendly_international_date_set (0x5cb9b0) names its parameters (day, month, duration) but they are written to +0/+1/+2 = weekday, day, month (build_international_date_table passes semana, dia, mes); its header 'day, month, span, year' is wrong the same way: header row in the TSV; the parameter rename (day->weekday, month->day, duration->month, year->year_offset) is a code change left to the caller.

evidence: day_match::SUMMARY (+0x5f) is the 0xd7a-byte match summary created at the end of the match (match_day.rs 231/286, 1389/1462) and passed to match_stats_record_match; its destructor is match_team_pair_destructor (it holds the two team objects). +0x5b is the 0x11d-byte humans' network scoreboard (match_day.rs 414, 503-551, 1525). The field names are right; the header called the scoreboard 'the summary'.

item: match_day::find_record_fixture: "+0 competition, +4 club" but match_stats_entry +0 = HOME_CLUB_ID
evidence: match_screens.rs 2550-2554 writes the 12-byte entry: +0 home club id, +4 away club id (match_stats_entry::AWAY_CLUB_ID), +8 day, +0xa year. In find_record_fixture +0 goes as the 5th argument of FixtureManager::find_fixtures, which is the club filter (fix_man.rs 1384 and match_man.rs 1426 pass a club id there; the competition goes as the 7th, here -1 = any, as friendly.rs 203 shows). So the search is the home club's fixtures that day in any competition, and +4 (the away club) picks the one.

item: scout_manager::send_scout_report_news: header +0xc of each record, body reads p + SCOUT_NAME_REF + 0xc (+0x43): one is wrong; +0x1f "the scout" named scout_report::PLAYER_NAME_REF
evidence: DEFEITO REAL (introduced by f2281941, readability batch 43). Disassembly of 0x7f9a60 at 0x7f9bc8: `lea edi, [esi + 0x37]` then `mov edx, [edi + 0xc]`: the original reads p + 0xc, with p = r + 0x37 + 0x67 k. Up to bb757341 the Rust read `p + 0xc`; batch 43 turned it into `p + scout_report::SCOUT_NAME_REF + 0xc`, which adds 0x37 twice (r + 0x7a + 0x67 k). The news slot 'scout's staff index' of every record gets a wrong dword (for k = 2 beyond the 3 records). The header ('+0xc' relative to the record's SCOUT_NAME_REF) is right.
code_change: pr(&mut idx, read_usize(p + scout_report::SCOUT_NAME_REF + 0xc) as u32);  ->  pr(&mut idx, read_usize(p + 0xc) as u32); // p already points at the record's scout_report::SCOUT_NAME_REF
header_part: +0x1f: scout_report::PLAYER_NAME_REF is verified (fill_staff_name_ref(player, report + 0x1f) at 0x7b6f48); the header's 'the scout' for it is wrong: it is the scouted player. Header row in the TSV.
note: worth a sweep of batch 43 for the same pattern (a pointer already offset by a named field, read again with the same name).

item: fin_prm::update_wage_bill: writes +0xc with this.set_stages() because this is typed League (wrong type in code)

evidence: match_record::HOME_SHOTS (+0x127) and HOME_SHOTS_ON_TARGET (+0x128), read on the side's block (base = game + SIDE_SIZE × side); the formula: (shots − 10)/30 + (on target − 10)/30 + (shots − opponent's shots) × 0.02. The 'average of the ratings by age +0x1c4' is the average of the row ratings weighted by the minutes on the pitch (s2 += rating × minutes, rows at match_record::ROW_MINUTE_LEFT_PITCH): 'by age' was also wrong and is fixed in the same row.

nation +0x88 is NumberStaff (nation.dat, community; +0x86 NumberClubs). The body returns when the nation's number_staff() is <= 1000 (B team, exe::club_is_national_team) or <= 100 (senior team). It is a head count, not a ranking.

Neither is a match count.

The body walks .national_job()/.job_for_nation() (5/12 -> the team's club::MANAGER) and only then copies the national function into .job_for_club() for a person without a club job.
